generic_skills: Predicting outcomes and making reasoned decisions
Working with others to generate ideas
Looking for patterns and making generalisation
Talking confidently and explaining ideas/opinions clearly
Using a range of media to communicate ideas
Using mathematics to justify and support decisions
Using technology to create, manipulate and process information
Using technology to collaborate, communicate and refine work
Respectfully responding to people of all cultures
Appreciating ethnicity as a cradle for creativity and innovation
values: honesty, uphold and defend the truth at all times
justice and fairness in dealing with others
integrity; moral uprightness and sound character

topics.core_competency: The learner applies matrices to represent data for solving real-world problems.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: present data from real life scenarios using matrices for informed decision making. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
solve real life problems like resource allocation, financial management using matrices. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

must_cover: operations on matrices (addition, subtraction and multiplication)
simultaneous equations in 2 variables using Cramer's rule
simultaneous equations in 3 variables using Cramer's rule

suggested_learning_activities.description: In group discussions, learners review: i) matrix formation ii) the order of matrices iii)types of matrices iv)operations on matrices (addition, subtraction and multiplication).
Through field visits, learners collect and present data like type and number of library books or members of different school clubs in a matrix form using ICT tools or otherwise.
Through Think- Pair- Share, learners review the determinant of a 2X2 matrix.
Through group discussions, learners apply determinant method (Cramer’s rule) to solve simultaneous equations in two variables derived from real world contexts.
In groups, using inductive approach, learners discuss the determinant of a 3x3 matrix.
Through group discussions, learners explore how to solve simultaneous equations in 3 variables using Cramer’s rule (determinant method).
Individually, the learner uses the internet or other sources to investigate the application of matrices in real life.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they review properties of matrices, collect and present data in matrix form, noting learners’ ability to: i) listen attentively and with comprehension, ii) sort and analyse information, and iii)demonstrate justice and fairness in dealing with others.

Engage learners and gauge their ability to explore types of operations on and properties of matrices, guiding them with thought-provoking questions to foster insightful discussions on presenting data using ICT tools or otherwise.
Assess learners' written or ICT-aided work to check accuracy of the types of and operations on matrices, data presentation in matrix form.

Observe learners as they discuss determinant of matrices to solve simultaneous linear equations, noting learners’ ability to: i) use mathematics to justify and support decisions, ii) interact effectively with others, and iii) exhibit hard work for self-reliance.
Through thought-provoking questions, examine learners’ ability to apply matrix method in solving simultaneous equations in two and three variables.

Assess learners' written work to check: i) correctness of the calculation of the determinant of matrices, ii) accuracy of the determinant of matrices, iii) application of matrix method to solve simultaneous equations in two and three variables, and iv) use of the internet or other sources to investigate the application of Matrices in real life.

investigative_skills.text_verbatim: collect and present data like type and number of library books or members of different school clubs

suggested_uses: present data like type and number of library books or members of different school clubs in a matrix form using ICT tools
use the internet or other sources to investigate the application of matrices in real life

topics.core_competency: The learner applies concepts of quadratic equations to solve real-life problems in different contexts.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the relationship between the sum and product of the roots of quadratic equations in solving real-life problems. (k, u, gs, v/a)
solve real-life problems such as optimizing areas or maximizing profits, minimizing losses using concepts of quadratic equations. (k, u, gs, v/a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through group discussions, learners review factorisation and completing the square of quadratic expressions.
Using Think- Pair- Share, learners discuss how to interpret the sum and product of roots.
In groups, learners discuss and identify minimum/ maximum values by completing squares.
Individually, learners use the internet/ library or other sources to find out applications of quadratics in real life situations.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss sum and product of roots, focusing on their ability to: i) use imagination to explore possibilities ii) work with others to generate ideas iii) demonstrate justice and fairness for others.
Engage learners and judge their ability to carry out factorisation, completing the square of quadratic expressions and interpreting the sum and product of roots.
Assess the learners’ work to check the accuracy of completing the square. Evaluate their ability to correctly apply the relationships between roots and the general quadratic equation.

Observe learners as they discuss their work on optimization of quadratic functions. Focus on their ability to: i) take responsibility for own learning ii) interpret and interrogate mathematical data iii) show hard work and self-reliance.
Through conversation, prompt learners and establish their ability to obtain optimal values from quadratic functions.
Assess the clarity and accuracy of learners' written work on: i) maximum and minimum values of quadratic functions. ii) applications of quadratics in real life situations.

suggested_uses: use the internet/ library or other sources to find out applications of quadratics in real life situations

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses statistical measures to effectively interpret data from real-life contexts enabling them to make informed decisions.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine measures of relative position and data variability to make informed decisions in real-life contexts. (k, u, v/a, gs)
apply measures of dispersion to predict trends and make informed decisions in real-life contexts. (k, u, v/a, gs)

must_cover: measures of central tendency (mean, mode, median)
measures of relative position (percentiles, deciles, quartiles)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through group work and exploration, learners review: i) data types, ii) collection, classification and organization of data using frequency distribution tables, iii) estimation of measures of central tendency (mean, mode, median) iv) representation of data

In groups, learners analyse measures of relative position (percentiles, deciles, quartiles) through discussion and Hands on -Minds on activities to; i) assess data variability, ii) determine the use of relative positions in interpreting data distribution, and iii) identify value positions and apply these concepts to real-life scenarios like performance analysis and data comparison.
Using learning stations, learners analyse a data set to calculate the range, variance, standard deviation and explore how variability influences decision-making.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss measures of relative position and data variability, assessing their ability to; i) interact effectively with others, ii) listen attentively and with comprehension, and iii) exhibit social harmony.

Engage with learners and evaluate their ability to; i) organize and present data on measures of central tendency and ii) apply measures of relative position to interpret data distribution and identify specific value positions.

Assess learners' written work and focus on: i) correctness of constructed frequency distribution tables, ii) accuracy in computing measures of central tendency and relative location, and iii) interpretation of data, and ability to solve real-life problems.

Observe learners as they interpret and analyse mathematical data using measures of dispersion. Look for: i) evidence of hard work for self-reliance, ii) ability to plan and carry out investigations iii) sort and analyse information.
Engage learners in a discussion and examine their ability to analyse a data set, to calculate the range, variance, and standard deviation, and how variability influences decision-making.

Assess learners' written work, analysis reports and charts. Focus on learners’ ability to: i) interpret data and apply measures of dispersion to real-world scenarios ii) correctly calculate range, variance, and standard deviation and verify whether their conclusions are clear, logical and well-supported.

investigative_skills.text_verbatim: ability to plan and carry out investigations

topics.core_competency: The learner applies indices and logarithms to solve societal problems involving exponential relationships and scaling in various fields.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: solve real-world scenarios using laws of indices. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
interpret the solutions of logarithmic equations in linear form to address real-world contexts. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Using a Socratic circle, learners review: i) powers as indices, ii) the laws of indices, iii) the simplification of expressions; Engaging in discussions to deepen their understanding and explore real-world applications.
Through group discussions, learners solve real-world scenarios, such as exponential growth and decay, that reduce to quadratics, using the laws of indices and interpret the solutions within context.
In groups, learners explore the relationship between logarithms and indices, logarithmic notation and the laws of logarithms.
Through a Socratic circle, learners discuss how to apply laws of indices and logarithms in solving equations.

Learners apply concepts of indices and logarithms to real-world scenarios, such as exponential growth, decay, navigation, and music, through a project-based investigation, utilising online resources or other materials.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss indices and relate them to logarithms noting their ability to: i) plan and carry out investigations ii) talk confidently and explain opinions clearly, iii) exhibit justice and fairness in dealing with others.

Engage learners in a discussion and evaluate their ability to: i) solve equations that simplify to quadratics using the laws of indices; and ii) interpret their solutions of real-world scenarios such as exponential growth and decay.

Assess clarity and accuracy of learners written work as they apply the laws of indices to: i) solve real-world problems; ii) simplify equations to quadratics; and iii) interpret the solutions in contexts like exponential growth, decay, demonstrating application of these concepts.

Observe learners as they interpret solutions to logarithmic equations within real-world contexts, focusing on their ability to: i) interact effectively with others ii) work with others to generate ideas iii) hard work for self-reliance.

Engage learners in a dialogue and judge their ability to: i) solve logarithmic equations, ii) illustrate logarithmic notation iii) demonstrate the relationship between indices and logarithms, and their application to real-world problems

Assess learners' project work, ensuring accuracy in solving logarithmic equations and logical reasoning in interpreting solutions. Evaluate their ability to connect mathematical computations with real-world scenarios.

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: real-world scenarios, such as exponential growth, decay, navigation, and music

suggested_uses: utilising online resources or other materials

topics.core_competency: The learner applies principles and techniques of series to analyse trends and business problems to enhance decision-making skills.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: distinguish between Arithmetic and Geometric Progressions by recognising business related and financial applications. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
analyse business-related problems using arithmetic and geometric progressions. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

must_cover: sum of n terms of an AP and GP

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through group discussions, learners review pattern Identification, generation of sequences and number of terms in a sequence.
Learners explore the pattern obtained, to sum the terms of that sequence to form a series using common difference or common ratio.
In pairs, learners explore the definitions, formulas, and distinguishing features of each type of series, calculating terms, and determining whether the series are Arithmetic or Geometric.

In groups, learners discuss real-life financial scenarios such as instalment payments, interest growth, or pricing trends and identify whether these situations follow an arithmetic or geometric progression. They examine the patterns, discussing key differences. and share their findings in a class presentation.
Learners participate in a simulation where they act as financial advisors to a client with a specific financial goal (e.g., saving for a large purchase or planning for retirement).
Using both Arithmetic and Geometric Progressions, learners design different savings or investment plans, discussing which plan might be more suitable based on the client’s goals and timeline.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss arithmetic and geometric progressions, noting their ability to: i) interact effectively with others, ii) suggest and develop new ideas, and iii) exhibit justice and fairness in dealing with others.

In a conversation through quizzes and peer feedback, examine learners’ ability to: explore the differences between Arithmetic and Geometric series, nth term and sum of n terms of n terms of an AP and GP.
Assess learners’ written work for: i) correctness of nth term and sum of n terms of an AP and GP; and ii) accuracy in determining whether the series are Arithmetic or Geometric.

Observe learners as they discuss and apply arithmetic and geometric progressions in real-life, noting their ability to: i) use imaginations to explore possibilities, ii) predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions, and iii) exhibit creativity and innovation.
In a conversation, evaluate learners’ ability to discuss application of Arithmetic and Geometric Progression in real-life financial scenarios.

Assess the learners’ written work and ascertain proper application of the Arithmetic and Geometric progressions in real world scenarios such as investment growth and payment schemes and enhanced decision making.

topics.core_competency: The learner applies knowledge of permutations and combinations to solve problems related to counting, arranging, and selecting items in different fields.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: employ the knowledge of basic principles of counting in situations like sports team line-ups, library book displays, and line management during meal times to make informed decisions. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
apply the knowledge of permutations in arrangement of items, paying attention to the order, for effective organisation of events from real life situations. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
analyse the impact of different constraints in selection of items, for effective organization of events and activities. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

must_cover: arrangements in a row/line and circle

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners explore the basic principle of counting and how it is applied in arrangement of items to determine the number of ways in which a certain number of items can be arranged in a row/ line and circle.
Learners brainstorm on how to: i) relate the number of ways of arranging in a row/line and circle n unlike objects to n! ii) formulate examples and determine solutions using the formula n!
In groups, learners arrange sets of items in a specific order.
In groups, learners explore and determine the number of ordered arrangements, relating their findings to the formula nPr using simple examples.

In pairs, using various case studies, learners discuss how permutations are applicable in real life situations such as cryptography, programming, genetics and scheduling. Learners formulate and solve scenarios.

In different groups, learners: i) discuss how to deal with selections from different sets of items. ii) determine the number of selections and relate their findings to the formula nCr, examining simple examples to solidify their understanding.

After listening to guest speakers from relevant fields (e.g., a statistician, a computer scientist), in pairs learners discuss how combinations are applicable in real life situations. They formulate scenarios and practice finding solutions using the formula for combinations.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss basic principles of counting, with focus on learners’ ability to: i) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly ii) plan and carry out investigation iii) showcase respect for humanity and environment.
In a conversation, prompt and evaluate learners’ ability to: i) use the basic principle of counting ii) apply the principle in arrangement of items in a row/line and circle relating it with n!
Assess the learners’ written work and check for correctness of the calculations as they use the formula n!

Observe learners as they discuss arrangement of items paying attention to the order, with focus on how they: i) plan and carry out investigation, ii) listen attentively and with comprehension, and iii) exhibit justice and fairness in dealing with others.
In a conversation, examine the ability of learners to deal with different sets of items and make arrangements, paying attention to the order and relate their findings to the formula nPr
Assess the learners’ written work and check for correctness of formulated scenarios and the appropriate use of the formula nPr in solving problems.

Observe learners as they discuss selection of items from a set with focus on how they: i) plan and carry out investigation ii) identify problems and ways forward iii) showcase justice and fairness in dealing with others.
In a conversation, examine learners’ ability to select from different sets of items and relate their findings to the formula nCr.
Assess the learners’ written work or presentation and check for correctness of formulated scenarios and the appropriate use of the formula nCr in solving problems.

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses the effectiveness of moving averages and index numbers on prediction of trends of events and their impact on policy decisions.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: contrast between odd and even number of moving points to plot graphs of moving averages from real life situations. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
predict trends of events from graphs for informed decisions using real life scenarios. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
evaluate index numbers and make analysis to inform the placement of priorities in real life. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners explore the formulae and distinguish features of odd-point and even-point moving totals.
In pairs, learners explore the skills of: i) calculating odd and even moving point averages, and ii) drawing and interpreting graphs of moving averages.
In groups, learners discuss the application of graphs of moving averages in making predictions when planning and choosing priorities.

Learners through think-pair-share, explore the formulae and distinguishing features of: i) Simple Index numbers/relatives, ii) Simple Aggregate index, iii) Simple average/cost of living index, iv) Weighted average/cost of living, v) Value index, and vi) Weighted aggregate index.
In groups, learners calculate index numbers for different sets of data extracted from newspapers, internet etc, make analysis and predictions on trends of prices, consumption and the cost of living.
Individually, learners conduct a research project on the impact of inflation on a particular sector of the economy.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss odd point and even point moving totals and averages, noting their ability to: i) interact effectively with others ii) sort and analyse information iii)showcase justice and fairness in dealing with others.
In a conversation, examine learners’ ability to explore the differences between odd and even number of moving points.
Assess learners’ write ups to check correctness of: i) identification of the trend of events. ii) odd point and even point moving totals. iii) odd and even moving averages.

Observe learners as they discuss moving averages, noting their ability to: i) plan and carry out investigation ii) identify problems and ways forward iii)showcase justice and fairness in dealing with others.
In a conversation, judge learners’ ability to apply moving averages in real–life scenarios such as bond markets and risk management.
Assess the learners’ graphical drawing and ascertain the proper application of the moving averages in real world scenarios.

Observe learners as they discuss price indices, note their ability to: i) interact effectively with others, ii) listen attentively with comprehension, and iii)exhibit justice and fairness in dealing with others.

In a conversation, evaluate learners’ ability to: i) differentiate between simple price index, unweighted price indices/ simple aggregate price index and weighted price indices; and ii) calculate index numbers for different sets of data and make analysis on trends of prices, consumption and the cost of living.

Assess the learners’ written work and check for correctness of calculations and interpretation of: i) price relative, ii) simple price index number, iii) simple aggregate price index, iv) weighted average price index, v) weighted aggregate price index, vi) value index, and vii) cost of living index.

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: impact of inflation on a particular sector of the economy

suggested_uses: data extracted from newspapers, internet etc

topics.core_competency: The learner interprets data from real life scenarios to understand relationships between two variables in various contexts for decision making and prediction.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: interpret scatter graphs to visualise relationships and trends using real-world data from scientific experiments, economics, geography for prediction and decision making. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
analyse the type and strength of correlation between two variables for prediction and decision making (k, u, s, v/a, gs).

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners analyse a real-life case study involving two variables, such as study time and exam scores. They collect or simulate relevant data and organise it systematically.

Using Think-Pair-Share, learners represent the relationship between two variables through a scatter diagram with an appropriate scale and draw the line of best fit through the mean point to make predictions. (Learners can use visual tools)
In groups, learners interpret positive and negative correlations, such as between study time and exam scores, to make informed decisions and discuss the implications of their findings in the class.

Through think- pair and share, learners calculate the Spearman's rank correlation coefficient from a data set to assess the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables, such as student rankings in different subjects, study habits, and academic performance quantitatively.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they draw and interpret scatter graphs. Note their ability to: i) interact effectively with others ii) take responsibility for own learning, iii)demonstrate social responsibility.
Converse with the learners and examine their ability to analyse; i) the choice of scales, ii) plotted points, iii)relationship between two sets of data.
Give learners a task to also draw a line of best fit for prediction.

Assess learners’ written work for: i) correctness and logical organisation of the dataset. ii) a neatly constructed scatter graph with labelled axes and uniform scale. iii) a clear line of best fit. iv) accurate prediction.

Observe learners as they calculate the Spearman's rank correlation coefficient. Focus on their ability to: i) sort and analyse information ii) predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions iii)demonstrate creativity and innovativeness.

Converse with learners and judge their ability to: i) apply the formula for Spearman's rank correlation ii) assess the strength and direction of the relationship and the significance of their findings in the context of student rankings.

Assess the learners’ written report or analysis for: i) accuracy of Spearman's rank correlation calculation ii) accuracy of the results iii) correct explanation of the strength and direction of the relationship between the two variables.

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses vector concepts and operations to solve mathematical and physical problems in 2D spaces in various fields.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: perform operations to determine magnitude and direction in 2D spaces in real-world situations. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
analyses the dot product (scalar product) and angle between two vectors to solve problems in real-world contexts. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through think- pair and share, learners review; i) vector definitions, ii) vector notations, iii) position vectors, iv) displacement vectors, and v) vector algebra in 2D.
Learners work in groups to discuss scalar multiplication on vectors and utilise digital tools such as GeoGebra or Desmos to visualise the resulting changes.
Individually, learners explore magnitude and direction of a vector in 2D spaces and real-world situations like engineering, computer graphics design, and sports and present to the plenary
In groups, learners demonstrate how to compute dot product and angle between two vectors to solve problems in real-world contexts such as physics, engineering, and navigation.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss vector concepts in 2D noting their ability to: i) interpret and interrogate mathematical data ii) use technology to create, manipulate and process information iii)exhibit creativity and innovation.

Converse with learners and examine their ability to: i) present different vector notations, operations and apply scalar multiplication ii) apply magnitude and direction in 2D and real-world situations.

Assess learners’ work for: i) correct use of the digital tools to demonstrate a clear understanding of scalar multiplication on vectors. ii) correctness of vector algebra in 2D. iii) correctness of magnitude and direction of a vector.

Observe the learners as they discuss dot /scalar product and determine the angle between two vectors. Note learners’ ability to: i) work effectively in diverse teams, ii) work independently with persistence, and iii) showcase creativity and innovativeness.
Engage learners and evaluate their ability to apply dot product and angle between two vectors to real-life situations.
Assess learners’ written work to check for correct use of the dot product and the accuracy of the angle between two vectors.

suggested_uses: utilise digital tools such as GeoGebra or Desmos to visualise the resulting changes

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses trigonometric concepts to solve real-world problems in various fields.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: use trigonometric ratios and their reciprocals to solve right angled triangle problems in real-life contexts such as construction and navigation. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)
apply trigonometric identities to solve practical problems in fields such as physics and engineering. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)
Solve quadratic trigonometric equations to address real-world problems in contexts like engineering and architecture. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)

must_cover: trigonometric identities (sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, tan²θ + 1=sec²θ, cot²θ + 1 = cosec²θ)
sketching sin θ, cosθ and tan θ graphs

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through group discussions, learners review sine, cosine, tangent of an angle of any magnitude using the quadrants of a unit circle and trigonometric ratios of angles greater than 90⁰.
Individually, learners use the trigonometric ratios of sine, cosine, and tangent to determine their corresponding reciprocals and share with the class.
Using Think–Pair–Share, learners solve real-life problems involving trigonometric ratios such as determining the height of a wall using a ladder's angle and length, in construction contexts.

Through guided discovery, learners use a right-angled triangle to explore the sine, cosine and tangent ratios of the special angles (30°, 45°, and 60°) and solve trigonometric problems in real life scenarios.
Through Socratic circle, learners use the Pythagorean theorem and algebraic reasoning to derive Pythagorean trigonometric identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, tan²θ + 1=sec²θ and cot²θ + 1 = cosec²θ
In groups, learners explore how trigonometric identities simplify calculations and are an integral part to solving real world problems in various fields.
Using Think–Pair–Share, learners review the sketching of sin θ, cosθ and tan θ graphs and how the properties of the graphs assist in solving quadratic trigonometric equations.

In groups, learners engage in a guided inquiry activity to analyse a quadratic trigonometric equation, such as 2sin² θ − cosθ = 1, using factoring and trigonometric identities. They explore how these mathematical techniques are applied to real-world contexts, such as addressing engineering challenges in fields like construction and design.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they solve right angled triangle problems in real-life context noting how they: i) plan and carry out investigations, ii) identify problems and ways forward, and iii) show social responsibility.
Converse with learners and examine their ability to explore the sine, cosine and tangent ratios of the special angles (30°, 45°, and 60°) and solve trigonometric problems in real-life scenarios.

Assess the learners’ work. Look out for correctness of; i) a labelled diagram of the scenario, ii) a step-by-step calculation and explanation, and iii) the final answer and conclusion in relation to real-world scenarios.

Observe learners as they discuss and derive trigonometric identities, noting learners' ability to: i) evaluate different solutions ii) identify problems and ways forward iii)exhibit integrity; moral uprightness and sound character.

In conversation examine the learners’ ability to: i) derive trigonometric identities using the Pythagorean theorem and algebraic reasoning ii) explore the relationships between the identities and apply reasoning to prove their validity.
Assess learners’ written proofs of the trigonometric identities for correctness and how these identities are integral to solving real -world problems.

Observe learners as they solve quadratic trigonometric equations from real-world challenges noting their ability to: i) work effectively in diverse teams, ii) interact effectively with others, and iii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness.

Converse with learners and evaluate their ability to analyse the key features of sine and cosine graphs and how these features assist in solving quadratic trigonometric equations, with real-world applications.

Assess learners' written solutions. Focus on the correctness of: i) the quadratic trigonometric equation, including a step-by-step explanation, ii) a sketch graph, and iii) a reflection on how these concepts apply to real-world construction contexts.
